Why a button is slow to acquire
Larger and closer targets help, but the law is quantitative; measure distance and width.
Why a menu feels cognitively expensive
Reduce choices per level or add search; do not hide expert paths behind excess nesting.
Reduce extraneous load with segmentation and worked examples; intrinsic complexity remains.
Active recall feels harder than review but improves durable retention.
Why debugging speed varies by expertise
Build pattern libraries through feedback on real failure modes, not passive exposure.
Why a post-mortem becomes hindsight theater
Reconstruct what was knowable at the time, not what became obvious later.
Use reference classes, outside view, and pre-mortems rather than team confidence.
Whether a psychology claim is trustworthy
Prefer pre-registration, large N, multi-lab replication, and plausible effect size.
Why a team practice is not adopted
Defaults and peer norms help only when the practice genuinely reduces friction and preserves agency.
